newsitem.title: USA: Gannett says income soars 30 pct; E.W. Scripps net up 22 pct.
newsitem.headline: Gannett says income soars 30 pct; E.W. Scripps net up 22 pct.

text.p: Gannett Co., the multimedia giant, said Monday it earnings jumped nearly 30 percent in the second quarter, boosted by record results at its broadcasting unit.
At the same time, the E.W. Scripps Co. reported a 22 percent rise in earnings for the quarter but warned that higher newsprint prices may dampen its profit outlook over the next six months.

Gannett, publisher of 89 daily newspapers, including USA TODAY, and owner of 18 TV stations as well as five radio stations, said its earnings rose to $194.7 million, or $1.38 a share, vs. year-earlier earnings of $150.0 million, or 98 cents a share.
The Arlington, Va.-based company said its revenues rose to $1.18 billion from $1.10 billion.
Gannett said the newspaper unit's operating earnings increased to $263.5 million from $203.0 million and broadcasting income rose to $96.9 million from $82.1 million.
Gannett's stock was up $1.56 at $105.50 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
E.W. Scripps said it earned $38.6 million, or 48 cents a share, in the second quarter, up from $31.7 million, or 39 cents per share, a year earlier.
Revenues jumped to $305.5 million from $277.3 million.
E. W. Scripps said revenues from its entertainment units jumped 45 percent to $36.5 million, thanks to strong results at its cable network Home & Garden Television.
Newspaper revenues increased 8.9 percent to $182 million, while television revenues edged up 2.3 percent to $87.1 million.
The Cincinnati-based company said it was taking a "cautious approach" to its results in the upcoming months.

"Higher year-over-year newsprint prices will dampen profit growth at the newspapers in the second half of the year, and the absence of political advertising this fall will leave the TV stations scrambling to replace that revenue," said William R. Burleigh, president and chief executive officer.
"Also, while Home & Garden Television is developing at a faster rate than expected, we still project higher losses in the third and fourth quarters than in the first half of the year," he said.
E. W. Scripps' stock was up 12.5 cents at $43.1875 on the NYSE.
